summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of recurrent infections was admitted for abnormal lab results showing elevated liver enzymes, hyperkalemia, and acute kidney injury. She felt well without abdominal pain or systemic symptoms. The transaminitis was attributed to recent antibiotic and statin use, all of which were discontinued. Hyperkalemia resolved with kayexalate and IV fluids, and kidney function stabilized. Liver enzymes improved during the stay, and no imaging was needed. She remained on oral vancomycin for ongoing C. difficile treatment and continued her baseline medications. A urine culture showed yeast and probable Enterococcus, but without symptoms, no new treatment was started. The PICC line was noted to have migrated slightly but remained functional. She was discharged home with nursing services after a two-day stay, with instructions to follow up on liver tests and colorectal evaluation for persistent stool in the vaginal vault.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
